request.spec:
Each person's row shows, for every period, a carried figure: the due of their claims that count
which belong to a period ending before this period starts and were still OPEN or
PENDING at the end of this period (by the status log, as the period figures count). A period with
nothing carried shows 0.00.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each person's row shows, for every period, a carried figure: the due of their claims that count
which belong to a period ending before this period starts and were still OPEN or
PENDING at the end of this period (by the status log, as the period figures count). A period with
nothing carried shows 0.00.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now shows a carried figure for every period, next to that period's due-total, and all 4 acceptance tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The whole change is in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. A period's carried figure adds up a person's claims that:
- fall in an earlier period, one that ends before this period starts;
- were still OPEN or PENDING at the end of this period, going by the status log;
- still count under the rules the period due-totals already use, so deferred claims and open claims dated in a hold or after retirement are left out.

Each claim adds the same due amount it adds to its own period's figure. A period with nothing carried shows `0.00`. The value is in `person-period-<name>-carried`.

The server, the stored data and the audit file are unchanged. The existing period due-totals are worked out on screen from the loaded claims, and the carried figure is worked out the same way.

Decision for you: the carried figure is always worked out live, even for a closed or soft-closed period, whose due-totals are frozen when it closes. None of the tests close a period, so they don't check this. If you want it frozen at close as well, the server would need to save it when the period closes, the way it saves the due-totals now.
